dropped_turns.speaker: CON
dropped_turns.text: When a frightened person makes a harmful mistake, treating the act as a product of panic can lead us to help rather than simply condemn. That humane response proves abandoning free will improves judgment.

dropped_turns.speaker: PRO
dropped_turns.text: Helping rather than condemning does not prove the person lacked choice; it shows that wise responses consider causes and agency together. Compassion is fully compatible with responsibility, so your example never reaches free will.

turns.text: When a person understands two options and can act on either after weighing them, that person exercises free will. Causes supply materials for judgment; they do not settle the judgment beforehand.

turns.text: People use freedom in arguments about praise, punishment, and social rules. Those disputes matter, but labels for blame are not the question. The question is whether anyone could choose otherwise, and prior causes say no.

turns.text: Human beings author their lives through countless choices, even though some choices occur under severe limits. A cause can shape a decision without replacing the person's active role in making it.

turns.speaker: CON

turns.text: But doesn't your argument for every human choice is produced by prior causes fight your argument that this human choice is not produced by prior causes?
